original_question: For n >= 2, let psi_n be the infimum of |Gamma|/n! over all finite subgroups Gamma of GL(n, R) for which there exists a Gamma-superflow. Here a Gamma-superflow is a flow whose vector field is a nonzero vector field Q(x) = (Q_1, ..., Q_n) with 2-homogeneous rational components, invariant under Gamma by gamma^(-1) o Q o gamma = Q for all gamma in Gamma, and unique up to scalar among invariant vector fields of minimal common-denominator degree. Is it true that psi_n = 2 for every n >= 3?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 11 (“Superflows with the smallest possible symmetry group”).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the quantity psi_n, the ambient group GL(n,R), the existence of a Gamma-superflow as the admissibility condition, the 2-homogeneous rational vector-field requirement, the Gamma-invariance condition gamma^(-1) o Q o gamma = Q for all gamma in Gamma, the uniqueness-up-to-scalar versus larger common-denominator-degree condition, and the intended conclusion psi_n = 2 for all n >= 3.
missing_details: The paper introduces a Gamma-superflow via an exact (faithful) representation Gamma -> GL(n,R) and then identifies Gamma with its image; your draft starts directly from a finite subgroup Gamma <= GL(n,R).
The paper phrases the definition as a property of a flow phi together with its vector field Q, namely that Q is exactly the vector field of phi.

Your phrase “unique up to scalar among invariant vector fields of minimal common-denominator degree” is a faithful paraphrase, but the paper’s exact wording is comparative: every other Gamma-invariant vector field is either a scalar multiple of Q or has strictly higher degree of a common denominator.
The setup immediately before the open question records the known base case psi_2 = 2; this should be retained in a paper-faithful stand-alone version.
The paper’s open problem asks only about n >= 3; the definition of psi_n is given for general n.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 2, define psi_n to be the infimum of |Gamma|/n! over all finite subgroups Gamma of GL(n,R) for which there exists a Gamma-superflow. Here, a Gamma-superflow means a flow phi on R^n with vector field Q = (Q_1,...,Q_n) whose components are 2-homogeneous rational functions, such that gamma^(-1) o Q o gamma = Q for every gamma in Gamma, and such that every other vector field Q' satisfying the same invariance for all gamma in Gamma is either a scalar multiple of Q or has strictly larger degree of a common denominator than Q. Given that psi_2 = 2, is it true that psi_n = 2 for every n >= 3?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8 rather than any earlier problem in the paper. In that section the author first gives Definition 1 of a Gamma-superflow, then defines psi_n as the infimum of |Gamma|/n! over finite subgroups of GL(n,R) admitting a superflow, notes that psi_2 = 2 was proved in the cited superflow paper, and finally poses exactly Problem 11: whether psi_n = 2 for all n >= 3. No nilpotency condition, asymptotic quantifier, or hidden “for sufficiently large” clause appears in this problem; the essential hidden assumptions are only the real field, the faithful linear action, the 2-homogeneous rationality of the vector field, and the precise uniqueness criterion.
